page: Amazon Web Services m7g.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by a 64-core AWS Graviton3 processor based on the arm64 Neoverse-V1 architecture. Operating at 2.6 GHz with one physical thread per core, the configuration offers dedicated execution without virtualization overhead. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per core. Networking capabilities reach a 30 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The platform includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier capabilities in multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth. The architecture achieves top-decile performance in multi-core Clang software compilation and PassMark memory testing, complemented by uncached read throughput of 253.89 GB/sec. Multi-threaded evaluations such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core place within the top 25 percent of tested systems. Synthetic application tests demonstrate upper-quartile results in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the median distribution bracket.

The bare-metal setup maximizes hardware density and instruction efficiency across all 64 physical cores, eliminating hypervisor overhead. Tradeoffs include modest single-core execution speed and the absence of onboard disks, which may introduce latency dependencies on networked storage for disk-heavy tasks. The server is best suited for scalable web services, continuous integration build clusters, container infrastructure, in-memory caching nodes, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.

The hardware contains no onboard local storage or GPU accelerators.
